speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether he can provide an update on the number of dengue cases observed nationally and in Woodgrove constituency in the second quarter of this year; (b) what are the reasons for the high number of cases; and (c) what are the latest efforts to contain the spread of dengue.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the measures taken to reduce the instances of dengue fever have been yielding results; and (b) whether there are other reasons for the high number of cases so far.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA's gravitrap surveillance system has shown an increase in the Aedes aegypti mosquito population by almost three times since the last major dengue outbreak in 2013.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This persistently high Aedes aegypti mosquito population increases the risk of transmission of the dengue virus.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, the mean temperature for the first half of this year was 0.7 degrees higher than the same period last year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Warmer temperatures result in higher transmission of dengue due to the accelerated development of the Aedes mosquito and shorter incubation period of the dengue virus.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Due to our past successes in dengue prevention, the proportion of adults who have had dengue before has progressively decreased from 59% in 2004, to 51% in 2009, and 41% in 2017.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This results, however, in lower herd immunity among our population, and a large proportion of Singapore's resident population remains susceptible to dengue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA, together with agencies in the Inter-Agency Dengue Task Force and Town Councils, have stepped up housekeeping measures and inspections of common areas to eliminate potential breeding areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sixty percent of the breeding habitats detected were found in residential premises.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If we look at the dengue clusters, the proportion of breeding habitats detected in residential premises is even higher at 70%.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This points to an urgent need for home and premises owners to step up their efforts to eradicate mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA will enforce against premises owners found with mosquito breeding and has taken about 1,200 enforcement actions against households between January and June.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since the launch of the National Dengue Prevention Campaign in April, 89 divisions across Singapore have organised more than 1,000 dengue prevention events and activities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mayors, grassroots advisers, community leaders and dengue prevention volunteers have been visiting homes to share dengue prevention tips, including information on how to identify potential mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To heighten the public's awareness and vigilance against mosquito breeding and dengue, dengue cluster alert banners, posters and notices have also been strategically placed around the estate in dengue cluster areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Poster walkers have been deployed and dengue prevention advertorials have been displayed at high footfall areas within clusters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA has also reached out to the public through TV and radio commercials, as well as digital and social media platforms, such as Facebook and Instagram.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are seeing positive outcomes from these collective efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This weekly number of dengue cases has also come down from a high of 664 cases in the second week of July to the current 478 cases in the third week of August.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some of the largest clusters in Woodlands, Upper Thomson, Chai Chee and Pasir Ris have closed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA will continue to work with our partners to enhance the efforts in dengue control.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: From the second half of 2019, NEA will progressively deploy an additional 14,000 Gravitraps to new Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks and landed estates.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will augment NEA's current network of 50,000 Gravitraps and enhance our surveillance capabilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Gravitrap surveillance system allows NEA to prioritise its resources and deploy officers to focus on areas with high mosquito population.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, since 25 August, NEA has partnered the People's Association (PA) to step up dengue outreach.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Five thousand volunteers from PA grassroots organisations and Community Emergency and Response Teams (CERTs) will work hand in hand with dengue prevention volunteers to conduct house visits and distribute dengue prevention leaflets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Another new initiative by NEA is the sharing of information on areas with relatively higher Aedes aegypti adult mosquito population on its webpage to facilitate targeted action by key stakeholders, community partners and residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The information aims to increase awareness of dengue risk in areas with high mosquito population which might not yet be dengue clusters, so that stakeholders can pre-emptively take measures to reduce potential mosquito breeding habitats and avoid the formation of new dengue clusters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While the results from Project Wolbachia field studies have shown promise, the Wolbachia technology has only been tested in small study sites in Singapore and remains under research and development.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is important for NEA to evaluate the technology rigorously before deploying it on a larger scale.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA's approach to Project Wolbachia is aligned with the World Health Organization's and the International Atomic Energy Agency's guidelines on developing sterile insect technologies using a phased approach.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Each phase of Project Wolbachia has a clearly defined objective to progress the study and evaluate the technology systematically.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The project is now in Phase 3, which aims to determine if the Aedes aegypti population suppression achieved thus far can be sustained in larger areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As field studies require prior systematic design, preparation and historical data for comparison, they are not suited for reacting to current dengue clusters, which are very dynamic.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It will not replace the community's efforts to ensure good housekeeping, which is still needed to keep our homes and estates free from mosquitoes and dengue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The region around us is similarly seeing an upsurge in dengue cases this year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need to remain vigilant and continue to work as a community to suppress the Aedes mosquito population and keep dengue cases in check.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I urge everyone to join in the collective effort to stop the dengue transmission cycle by regularly doing the five-step Mozzie Wipeout and to remind your family members, friends and neighbours to remove stagnant water from within and around their homes.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of my residents are understandably very concerned and many of my residents have asked why fogging is being carried out infrequently as opposed to the past.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I mentioned just now, in areas where there are higher incidences of dengue fever, 70% of the breeding is found in homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, even if we carried out more fogging, residents will usually close their windows anyway.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, the best way to prevent dengue from proliferating is to destroy their habitats and most of them are within homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Yes, we can and we must, to kill the adult mosquitoes outside.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is no silver bullet in whichever method we choose and we cannot just use one method to stop this problem.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, is there any discernible difference in terms of breeding sites and residents contracting dengue in private estates and HDB estates?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For public housing, some of them are found in common areas and the Town Councils must and should take all precautions possible to prevent breeding and mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some of these places are really hard to access.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Whereas for private housing, most of the breeding places, in addition to being found within homes, are also found in their gardens, usually in pots which are not probably treated or pots which collect water.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For cases of dengue contracted overseas, as I had mentioned, our region is now suffering from a spike in the number of dengue cases.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, as we travel, please take the necessary precautions, put on insect repellent on yourselves and, especially on your children, so that they do not get bitten by mosquitoes and inadvertently contract dengue.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What measures are being taken to deal with this issue?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Generally speaking, it has not been difficult to access homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When our NEA inspectors knock on doors, they would open the doors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But sometimes, there is nobody at home, or sometimes, it could be an elderly at home.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we try very hard to work with the neighbours to find out how we can get access.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Particularly for areas which are dengue clusters, we do not wait long.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will try to gain entry, and NEA has the powers to do so.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to commend the very diligent NEA ground staff and, of course, the volunteers who walk the blocks and flats with them to educate and to warn residents about dengue prevention.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As the Minister mentioned, most of the mosquito-breeding habitats are inhouse.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We found that, on the ground, many of the NEA staff and the volunteers are very helpless when residents refuse to let them gain entry, sometimes out of non-cooperation, but a lot is also out of fear of the fine, the stick, thinking that when they open the doors, if they would be punished.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I was wondering if NEA could consider to, first, issue a severe warning, get entrance to the flat, check the premises and then, install the fine only from the second time that they visit.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is a lot of worry, fear and anxiety about someone coming to your house, inspecting your premises and then, punishing you straightaway, when you are not yet educated or aware.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am quite sure if you go through some Hansard reports, this question had been asked before: can we first give a warning, then issue the fine later, be kind?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think if dengue does not cause death, we probably could do that.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But dengue is known to cause death, and these could be our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think everyone has to be responsible and accountable to take care of their homes, to make sure they do not breed mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When NEA officers and dengue volunteers go in to check their homes, they are trying to help and also point out where possible breeding habitats could be found, and then, if found, they fine them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That sends a strong signal to everybody to take this seriously.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We never know which breeding habitat will produce the mosquito that may kill somebody we love.
